meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued
facts.summary: Maryland: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
facts.evidence_quote: each employer shall pay an employee or the authorized representative of an employee all wages due for work that the employee performed before the termination of employment, on or before the day on which the employee would have been paid the wages if the employment had not been terminated.

facts.value: on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued
facts.summary: Maryland: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on or before the day the wages would have been paid had employment continued.
facts.evidence_quote: each employer shall pay an employee or the authorized representative of an employee all wages due for work that the employee performed before the termination of employment, on or before the day on which the employee would have been paid the wages if the employment had not been terminated.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Maryland basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Maryland does not require reporting of independent contractors (per OCSE).
facts.evidence_quote: Independent Contractor Reporting Required?: No my state does not require independent contract reporting as legislation has not been passed for this to be a mandate.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide (updated 05/27/2026).

facts.value: Within 20 days of the employee's first day of work
facts.summary: Maryland: report a new hire within 20 days of the employee's first day of work.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: This is not received by Maryland New Hires any longer. It is not accepted either.
facts.source_title: Maryland Code, Labor and Employment, Section 8-626.1
facts.notes: Md. Code, Lab. & Empl. 8-626.1(b); 'beginning employment' is defined as the date the employee commences working. The OCSE guide entry for this element contains unrelated text, so the statute is the primary source.

facts.summary: Maryland: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Bi-weekly; Semi-monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Maryland is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Maryland base new employer UI rate: 2.60%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.summary: Maryland experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.30% to 7.50%.

facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law.
